tone.says: Bearth & Link 1980 posit phonemic contour tones for Wobe with features [Rise], [Fall], [Concave] besides [High], [Low], [Extreme]; Singler argues that an analysis using only level tones at the phonemic level (surface glides decomposed into level-tone sequences) succeeds where the contour-feature account fails — i.e. Wobe's 14 surface tones derive from sequences of 4 level tones.

sources.citation: Bearth, Thomas & Christa Link. 1980. The tone puzzle of Wobe. Studies in African Linguistics 11(2): 147-207.
sources.note: Nothing. Tao dialect (Kouibly area). p.148: syllable structure C1(C2)V1(V2)(V3), 14 contrastive tones on CV monosyllables, 'We will tentatively take the vowel as the unit of tone placement'; sections on tone distribution, F0 realization (mingograms) and morphotonology. The words stress/accent/prominence never occur in a prosodic sense (a full-text search for stress/accent the text: 'stress' only as a verb, pp. 165, 171).

sources.citation: Link, Christa and Bearth, Thomas (1980). The tone puzzle of Wobé. Studies in African Linguistics 11. pp. 147-207.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.quote: Before pause, monosyllabic items of type C(C)V have the possibility of 14 different tone patterns, bisyllabic morphemes of type C(C)V1V2 twenty-four, and trisyllabic morphemes of type C(C)V1V2V3 twelve. We will tentatively take the vowel as the unit of tone placement. Of the 14 tones possible on CV syllables, four are level tones (but cf. 3.3 and 3.6), five are rising, four falling and one rising-falling. [p. 148] ... very high 1 / high 2 / mid 3 / low 4 / (extra-low 5 occurs only in the combinations listed above); rising tones: 31, 32, 41, 42, 43; falling tones: 15, 25, 35, 45; rising-falling tone: 435. [p. 149] ... We arrive therefore at the conclusion that in Wobe a coherent analysis of the facts leads us to postulate the existence of 14 tonemes. In spite of the marked tendency of the extreme registers towards contoured realizations, there is very little doubt as to the pertinence of four registers. ... we are forced to admit the existence of irreducible contour tones which are impossible to describe in a satisfactory way as sequences of two level tones. [p. 186]
sources.locator: printed pp. 148-149 (section 0 Introduction and 1.1), p. 164 (Diagram 1, section 3.1), p. 186 (section 4.6 Summary)
sources.note: No catalog entry (in_catalog false). Lexical tone system: four level registers (very high 1, high 2, mid 3, low 4; extra-low 5 only as the endpoint of falls) plus unitary contour tonemes, 14 tonemes on short CV monosyllables (4 level, 5 rising 31 32 41 42 43, 4 falling 15 25 35 45, 1 rising-falling 435); 24 patterns on CVV bisyllables, 12 on CVVV. Tone-bearing unit tentatively the vowel (p. 148). Features proposed: [+-High], [+-Low], [+-Extreme] (height), [+-Concave], [+-Falling] (modulation) (p. 186). Phonetic notes: tones 2 and 3 are the only invariably level realizations; tone 1 is phonetic
sources.venue: Studies in African Linguistics 11
